cards.head: Critical cyber threat: AI firm Anthropic warns AI worms may soon reach smart TVs.
cards.body: Anthropic's testers say these AI worms may be months away and hard to switch off. Homes and small firms would likely be hit first; no such attack has happened yet.

report_refs.excerpt: AI company Anthropic warns that self-copying AI programs could be only months away from being able to copy themselves onto smart home devices such as ovens, televisions and security cameras.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / Nvidia China
cards.head: Chip maker Nvidia's China AI chip share fell to about a third this year.
cards.body: Research firm IDC estimates Huawei is now close behind Nvidia in China's data centres. Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, blames US export limits for handing the market to Huawei.

report_refs.excerpt: Nvidia's share of China's AI chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026 as Huawei and other Chinese makers gained ground, research firm IDC estimates.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / Investor day
cards.head: AI firm Anthropic reportedly shows big funds its finances for the first time today.
cards.body: Two unnamed sources say the meeting comes ahead of a possible stock market listing. The figures could show how fast the company grows and whether it profits.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic is reportedly set to show institutional investors its third-quarter financial results for the first time, at a meeting on 14 October ahead of a possible share listing.

cards.cat: Energy and infrastructure / ASML sold out
cards.head: ASML, the Dutch maker of chip-printing machines, cannot fully meet AI demand to 2028.
cards.body: Customers already discuss orders for 2029, says ASML chief executive Christophe Fouquet. If ASML is right, the machines stay scarce and AI services could stay costly.

report_refs.excerpt: ASML, the Dutch maker of chip-making machines, says AI-driven demand for its machines is so strong that it will not be able to fully supply its customers in 2027 or 2028.

cards.head: Oregon's governor halted pollution permits for new data centres until mid-2027.
cards.body: Governor Tina Kotek's letter would pause most large data centre building in the state. Amazon warned of lost jobs, and the pause rests on a letter, not a law.

report_refs.excerpt: Oregon's governor has ordered state environmental regulators to stop issuing air and water pollution permits for new or expanding data centers until July 2027, which would effectively pause most large data center building in the state.

cards.head: US safety officials weigh a claim that Tesla's robotaxis speed in school zones.
cards.body: An unnamed petitioner says the driverless cars break speed limits while school zones are active. If true, children near schools are at risk, but nothing has been proven yet.

report_refs.excerpt: US auto safety regulators say they are weighing a petition that claims Tesla's driverless taxis exceed the speed limit in active school zones.

cards.head: Digit robot maker Agility Robotics cleared a US step toward a stock market listing.
cards.body: Owners of a listed shell firm will vote on 2 November on merging with Agility. Agility says it would be the only listed US firm solely making working humanoid robots.

report_refs.excerpt: Agility Robotics, maker of the Digit humanoid robot, has cleared a key US regulatory step toward becoming a listed company through a merger with a blank-check firm.

cards.head: Meta launched Muse Wonder, AI models an independent ranking puts near the very top.
cards.body: Ranking group Artificial Analysis puts the larger one second, after AI firm Anthropic's model. Developers can use Muse Wonder now; its safety report and paid app version come later.

report_refs.excerpt: Meta has launched Muse Wonder, a new family of AI models whose larger version an independent ranking places second only to one Anthropic model.

cards.cat: Models and tools / Build your app
cards.head: Google now lets US adults run apps they made with AI on their Android phones.
cards.body: People describe an app to Google AI Studio, which builds it, then run it privately. The apps stay out of public listings and must still follow Google Play's rules.

report_refs.excerpt: Google now lets adults in the US run apps they built with AI on their own Android phones through Google Play, without publishing them to the public store.

cards.head: China has far more AI researchers than the US and keeps more graduates at home.
cards.body: Scott Singer, an analyst at US think tank the Carnegie Endowment, puts China months behind. Far fewer advanced chips and much less investment hold Chinese AI back.

report_refs.excerpt: Nature reports that China now has far more active AI researchers than the United States and keeps more of its own AI graduates at home than before, but is still estimated to trail the US frontier by three to seven months.

cards.head: An OpenAI engineer is charged with hiding a recording device in an executive room.
cards.body: OpenAI says its AI helped find him, and it fired him and alerted the FBI. US officials call it a national security threat; OpenAI sees no sign code was taken.

report_refs.excerpt: An OpenAI engineer has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in an executive conference room, which officials say was meant to capture sensitive talks about the company's technology.

cards.head: Johns Hopkins Medicine and AI firm OpenEvidence plan to reshape how doctors train.
cards.body: The plans include AI that weighs fresh evidence with each patient's own history. No dates, costs or results were given, so these are aims, not working tools.

report_refs.excerpt: Johns Hopkins Medicine and OpenEvidence, a medical AI company, have announced a partnership to redesign how doctors are trained and to build AI systems for patient care.

cards.head: Supermarket chain Kroger will cut 3,000 office jobs as it uses more tech and AI.
cards.body: Kroger's chief executive Greg Foran told staff it must cut work done twice. The cuts run over three years, and no teams or dates have been named yet.

report_refs.excerpt: Kroger, the biggest standalone US supermarket chain, says it will cut 3,000 corporate jobs over three years as it uses more technology and AI.

cards.head: Character.ai, a chatbot app sued over harm to children, has filed for bankruptcy.
cards.body: Character.ai plans a court-supervised sale by year end, and keeps the app running meanwhile. With no good bid, the app closes, leaving over 20 million monthly users without it.

report_refs.excerpt: Character.ai, the chatbot app that has faced lawsuits over harm to teenagers, has filed for bankruptcy and says Disney agreed to pay $20 million to license some of its intellectual property.

cards.head: Today's fun fact: a day of OpenAI's always-on AI helper costs about a latte.
cards.body: In security firm Geordie's test, the helper, dot, ran 155 jobs in one day unasked. Hanah-Marie Darley, Geordie's chief AI officer, likens the day's bill to a latte.

report_refs.excerpt: A security company found that OpenAI's always-on dot assistant used more than 300,000 tokens in a day without being asked.

entries.head: Hundreds of scientists asked for a world body to set safety rules for hacking-capable AI.

report_refs.excerpt: Hundreds of scientists signed an open letter asking for an international body to set safety rules and report incidents for advanced AI that can carry out cyberattacks.

entries.head: OpenAI and Anthropic told British lawmakers that AI safety rules should be binding.

report_refs.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic told a committee of British MPs that voluntary safety pledges are no longer enough and that binding rules are needed, while Google DeepMind and Meta would not back new laws.

entries.head: Chatbots missed emergencies far more in Vietnamese than in English in a simulated test.

report_refs.excerpt: A conference study found that four AI chatbots failed to advise emergency care in about 41% of simulated digestive-health emergencies described in Vietnamese, against 15% in English.

entries.head: Ex-US vice president Kamala Harris warned that time for AI safety limits is running out.

report_refs.excerpt: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris has warned in Seoul that the chance to put safety limits on AI is closing and has urged the United States to work with China on AI rules.

cards.head: AI chip shares keep falling as rising interest rates threaten the AI building boom.
cards.body: Chip-machine maker ASML can't fully meet demand, yet chip shares fell on rate fears. Watch TSMC's results on 15 October for demand; not financial advice.

report_refs.excerpt: The International Monetary Fund says in its latest world outlook that AI investment is holding up growth, and that a steep fall in it, a longer Middle East war or rising debt could weaken the economy.
AI chip stocks fell sharply again on Tuesday, with South Korea's main index down more than 6%, in what Reuters calls the strongest sign yet that the AI trade is turning.
Anthropic is reportedly set to show institutional investors its third-quarter financial results for the first time, at a meeting on 14 October ahead of a possible share listing.
ASML, the Dutch maker of chip-making machines, says AI-driven demand for its machines is so strong that it will not be able to fully supply its customers in 2027 or 2028.

Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, has said price rises from the AI building boom are spreading beyond data-centre supplies and he fears they reflect overheating demand.

cards.notice: General news and commentary. Not financial advice or an investment recommendation.

If this adds value to your day, share it with someone who should know. Thank you, and see you tomorrow.
